matches.rationale: Both identify the Adult dataset dimension inconsistency in Section 4. GT notes n=6 vs the known 14 features; pred_id 1 documents the same contradiction ('n=14' vs 'n=6' vs '6×6 Adult matrix') within the experimental section.

Both identify inconsistent gap conditions (strict vs non-strict inequality) across theorem statements and lemmas. GT notes the ambiguity between ≤ and < in Theorem 2.1, proof construction, and Lemma 3.1; pred_id 7 documents the same issue across Lemma 3.1 (δ_p > 5‖E‖ vs 4‖E‖ < δ_p) and Theorems 2.1–2.3.

GT identifies missing specification of how scaling factors multiply noise (raw entries vs final norm). No finding addresses this specific experimental protocol ambiguity about noise scaling methodology.

GT critiques the Abstract's 'up to √n improvement' claim as misleading without specifying restrictive conditions. No finding addresses this specific overclaim about the improvement factor's generality.
GT identifies fabrication of '[29, Remark 5.3]' (only [30] has such a remark). Pred_id 4 notes missing references [47]–[50], not the misattribution of Remark 5.3 between [29] and [30].
GT critiques the rhetorical choice of 'resolve' as overstating completeness. Pred_id 12 questions 'first-ever' novelty claims but does not address the 'resolve' language or its promotional nature.

GT identifies the implausibly large eigengap δ_p ≈ 37.02 for Adult dataset as likely fabricated. Pred_id 1 notes dimension inconsistencies but does not question the reported eigengap value's plausibility.

GT identifies ambiguity in Theorem 2.3 about whether max is over boundary or interior of Γ_1. Pred_id 6 addresses a different issue (arithmetic error in M_2 bound in Appendix F), not the max ambiguity.

Both identify misleading comparison to Mangoubi–Vishnoi bounds. GT notes the gap conditions differ (not apples-to-apples); pred_id 11 documents inconsistent descriptions of [29,30]'s gap conditions (4‖E‖ vs 2‖E‖, δ_p vs δ_i) across text and table.

GT critiques non-standard preprocessing and lack of reporting on excluded datasets or tested configurations. No finding addresses selective reporting of preprocessing configurations or dataset exclusions.
Both identify the strict vs non-strict inequality inconsistency across Theorem 2.1 statement, proof construction, and Lemma 3.1. This is the same cross-section inconsistency documented in pred_id 7.

Both identify contradiction between claims of tight/near-perfect bounds and actual empirical results. GT notes selective presentation hiding outliers; pred_id 9 documents Abstract's 'near-perfect tracking' vs Table 2's 88× ratio.
GT identifies misattribution of the bootstrapping technique to [38]. No finding addresses this specific reference fabrication about the bootstrapping argument's origin.
GT critiques Conclusion's claim of 'extending EYM' without acknowledging restrictive gap assumption. No finding addresses this specific overclaim about the scope of the EYM extension.

Both identify promotional language overstating empirical validation strength. GT critiques 'confirm' and 'closely track' without quantification; pred_id 9 documents the same issue ('near-perfect tracking' vs actual 88× ratio).
